SQL:
WITH _base AS (
  SELECT
    customers.tier AS "customers.tier",
    COUNT(*) AS "customers.customers",
    COUNT(DISTINCT customers.id) AS "customers.cd"
  FROM customers AS customers
  GROUP BY
    customers.tier
), _cm_customers__orders__amount_sum AS (
  SELECT
    customers.tier AS "orders.customers.tier",
    CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.amount_sum"
  FROM orders AS orders
  LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
    ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
  GROUP BY
    customers.tier
)
SELECT
  _base."customers.tier",
  _base."customers.customers",
  _base."customers.cd",
  _cm_customers__orders__amount_sum."orders.amount_sum" AS "customers.revenue"
FROM _base
LEFT JOIN _cm_customers__orders__amount_sum
  ON _base."customers.tier" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM _cm_customers__orders__amount_sum."orders.customers.tier"
LIMIT 21

args.message: Customer counts and revenue by tier. All 202 customers are counted, including those with no orders, and revenue is each customer's order amounts added up. Bronze has 100 customers with $163,987.18 in revenue, silver has 59 with $96,891.01, and gold has 43 with $71,294.79. Revenue includes orders of every status, including the ones marked "bad". Some orders point to customer IDs that aren't in the customer list (IDs go up to 9002), and those are left out.
